details:
NOVA: Astronaut POV — Space Mission Design Game

NOVA is an immersive 3D educational game that transforms space mission design into an interactive adventure. Players step into the role of astronauts and mission commanders, making decisions that determine the success of scientific missions. Guided by ORION, a virtual mission assistant, they learn how space technology works through exploration, experimentation, and problem-solving.

How does our project work?

NOVA offers two main experiences:

1. Protect Earth — Mission Morocco

Players discover how satellites can help address environmental challenges affecting Morocco, including droughts, wildfires, flash floods, and agricultural heat stress. Using NASA scientific resources such as FIRMS, GPM, SMAP, GRACE-FO, and Landsat, they explore how Earth-observation data helps scientists monitor environmental conditions.

Players select a threat, design an observation mission, choose satellite instruments, plan orbital coverage, manage resources, and decide how scientific information can support local communities. An interactive satellite-scanning activity makes the learning experience more engaging.

2. Explore the Unknown — Planetary Voyage

Players embark on missions to explore celestial destinations such as the Moon, Mars, Europa, and Titan. They design spacecraft, select materials, scientific instruments, propulsion and communication systems, plan trajectories, and overcome unexpected challenges.

Throughout the game, players must balance engineering constraints such as mass, power, budget, safety, mission duration, and data transmission. Every decision has consequences, encouraging players to reconsider their choices and improve their mission designs.

What tools and technologies did we use?

We developed NOVA using Claude AI and HTML. Claude was our primary AI-assisted development tool, helping us transform our ideas, scientific research, and creative vision into a functional, interactive browser-based game.

Our team developed the concept, researched NASA resources, designed the mission scenarios, defined gameplay mechanics, and tested and refined the experience.

This approach allowed us to combine human creativity and scientific thinking with AI-assisted development, demonstrating that innovative educational experiences can be created without advanced programming experience.

What makes NOVA creative?

NOVA goes beyond traditional educational games by combining first-person astronaut exploration, immersive 3D environments, interactive spacecraft engineering, and real-world environmental challenges.

Our most distinctive idea is connecting two purposes of space technology: exploring other worlds and protecting our own planet.

Players do not simply read scientific information. They experience challenges, make strategic decisions, observe their consequences, and learn from mistakes. ORION provides guidance throughout the adventure, making complex concepts easier to understand without overwhelming players.

The game also supports individual exploration and collaborative decision-making, highlighting the importance of teamwork in real space missions.

What benefits and impact do we aim to achieve?

Our goal is to make space science and engineering more accessible, engaging, and inspiring, especially for young people and students.

NOVA encourages critical thinking, creativity, teamwork, and problem-solving while introducing players to aerospace engineering and NASA scientific resources.

Our team considered several important factors throughout development: scientific credibility, educational value, accessibility, user experience, engineering realism, and entertainment. We wanted to create a game that remains understandable for beginners while offering meaningful challenges for more experienced players.

Ultimately, NOVA demonstrates that space exploration is not only about discovering distant worlds. It is also about using scientific knowledge and technology to better understand Earth and support communities.

Through NOVA, we hope to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and explorers by showing that every great mission begins with curiosity, creativity, and a decision.
